title: 1956 AHSME Problem 36
statement: If the sum \(1+2+3+\cdots+K\) is a perfect square \(N^2\) and if \(N\) is less than \(100,\) then the possible values for \(K\) are:

solutions.text:
The condition is \[ \frac{K(K+1)}2=N^2, \] or \[ (2K+1)^2-8N^2=1. \] The positive solutions of this Pell equation are generated from the fundamental solution \(3+\sqrt8.\) Their first pairs \((2K+1,N)\) are \[ \begin{aligned} &(3,1),\ (17,6),\\ &(99,35),\ (577,204),\ldots \end{aligned} \] Thus the values with \(N\lt100\) are \(K=1,8,49.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Generate successive positive solutions by multiplying \((2K+1)+N\sqrt8\) by \(3+\sqrt8,\) stopping when \(N\ge100\)
